title: Creditor Rights and Strategic Default: Evidence from India
abstract: I examine whether higher creditor rights prevent strategic default. Borrowers who cross either of two thresholds are exempt from a creditor rights law in India. Using a loan day-level dataset, I ﬁnd that loan performance is better when the law applies and that outperformance increases after a further rise in creditor rights. To discern the strategic motive, I use an unprecedented invalidation of the Indian currency whereby holders of high-value currency were forced to declare their cash holdings to banks. Defaulters exempt from the law showed a greater tendency to repay their loans during the ban period.

summary.oneLiner: This paper suggests that stronger creditor rights reduce strategic defaults by Indian borrowers, particularly when they cannot hide liquid assets.
summary.overview: Strategic default occurs when a borrower chooses to stop paying back a loan even though they have the money to pay. This study examines whether stronger legal protections for creditors make such behavior less likely. By looking at how borrowers reacted to a mandatory currency exchange program in India, the author identifies that those protected by stricter laws were less likely to withhold payments they could afford to make.
summary.question: Do higher creditor rights prevent strategic default by borrowers?
summary.method: A comparative analysis using loan performance around specific regulatory thresholds and an exogenous shock created by a currency ban.
findings: Loan performance is better when creditor rights laws apply to the borrower.
Outperformance of loans increases following a further rise in creditor rights.

Borrowers exempt from creditor rights laws show a greater tendency to repay loans only when forced to disclose cash holdings during a currency ban, suggesting they were previously acting strategically.
summary.whyItMatters: The findings suggest that the efficacy of bankruptcy or debt recovery laws is highly dependent on a borrower's ability to hide assets and the legal tools available to lenders to overcome such information asymmetries.
